title: Surface a stranded close and stop the deployed tip moving during the live gate

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: CONDITIONAL — round 1. Audited 42a6a03 on main; working tree clean apart from .vscode/settings.json (out of scope, twenty-nine sprints running). Sprint file re-read fresh at audit time.

One demonstrated defect. Neither FAIL-level criterion tripped: nothing refuses on divergence, and the docs-only case is genuinely detected. But Req 2's own sentence — "must not report a sprint as open when another tree has closed it" — still fails on the one worktree flow this framework mandates, and I reproduced it end to end.

================================================================
BLOCKER — REQ 2. A CLOSE IN THE WORKTREE IS STILL INVISIBLE FROM
MAIN WHEN THE SPRINT WAS NEVER STARTED IN MAIN.
scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py:834-839 (state_divergence_warning)
================================================================

REPRODUCED, not reasoned about. Scratch repo, real second worktree, the exact order CLAUDE.md documents for Dev Team 2:

  main:      /sprint-new                    -> registry 'todo', NO state file
  main:      commit the bookkeeping         (the commit rule)
  main:      git worktree add               (/sprint-worktree, "before building")
  worktree:  start, qa1, dev-done, ship, liveqa, complete

Worktree's own view:  Phase: complete
MAIN, /sprint-list:              "  1  todo         Dev Team 2 sprint"      no warning
MAIN, /sprint-status (no id):    "Sprint 1: Dev Team 2 sprint - todo"       no warning
MAIN, /sprint-status 1:          ERROR: No state file ... Run /sprint-start 1 first.

That third line is worse than silence: the one command with a per-sprint view dies before either divergence check runs, and tells you to start a sprint somebody already finished.

CAUSE, ISOLATED. Called the function directly against that same on-disk data:

  main state file exists : False
  main registry status   : todo
  wt   registry status   : done
  wt   state phase       : complete

  state_divergence_warning(1, this_registry_status='todo', other_roots=[wt]) -> None
  state_divergence_warning(1)                                               -> None
  CONTROL, same data, this_phase supplied instead of derived:
    -> "WARNING: sprint 1's state here reads phase 'dev_build' ... 1 other worktree
        disagree: <wt> (phase 'complete', registry status 'done')"

So the comparison logic is right and the message is right. The early return is what swallows it:

    if this_phase is None:
        this_state_path = state_path(sprint_id)
        if not this_state_path.exists():
            return None          # <- bails before the registry is ever looked at

cmd_new writes the registry entry and no state file (verified: zero write_state calls in cmd_new). cmd_start writes the state file wherever it runs. So for every sprint whose worktree is created before /sprint-start — which is what "run once, before Dev Team 2 starts building" and "cd there before touching any files" describe — main has a registry entry and no state file for the sprint's entire life, and this function returns None on the first check for that whole window. The caller already handed it `this_registry_status`; the function throws that away.

Note the shape of the miss: the registry half of Req 1 is real code that never executes on this path. That's why the acceptance criterion says "state files *and* the registry are covered" — half of the pair is unreachable exactly where the other half is missing.

WHY THE SUITE DIDN'T CATCH IT. The Req 1/2 test runs start/qa1/dev-done/ship in the main sandbox BEFORE `git worktree add`, so main always has a state file. The setup encodes the assumption that fails. The fix needs a case in the other order — worktree created first, sprint started only inside it — or the same gap comes back.

FIX. Don't bail when the local state file is absent: treat this tree's phase as None and still compare registry status, which the caller already supplied. I checked the silence property survives that: a sprint that's 'todo' here and 'todo' there with no state file in either tree gives other_phase None (phase_differs False) and equal statuses, so it stays quiet. Separately, `/sprint-status <id>` should surface the divergence instead of dying with "Run /sprint-start N first" when another tree holds the state — that advice is actively wrong. Two changes, both local. Neither is a redesign.

SCOPE HONESTY: if Dev Team 2 instead runs /sprint-start in main and cds afterwards, main has the state file and the warning fires correctly. So this is one of two plausible readings of the documented order, not both. It is still the reading the worktree section's own words describe, and it is the reading under which Team Assignments' note — "this sprint fixes the invisibility of work done in Dev Team 2's own worktree" — is exactly false.

================================================================
WHAT IS GOOD, AND IT IS MOST OF IT
================================================================

REQ 1's FAIL CRITERION — NOT TRIPPED. Enumerated every call site of state_divergence_warning and _other_worktree_roots: lines 1128, 1161, 2583, all `print`. No die(), no sys.exit, no return-value branching. Nothing gates. Every failure mode collapses to None — no git, no other worktrees, unreadable or missing state/registry in the other tree. Correct, and matches sprint 13's discipline.

REQ 1's MESSAGE — names the other tree's resolved path, its phase, and its registry status. That is the actionable version, not "another tree disagrees."

REQ 3 — VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, in my own scratch repo with a real bare origin, not by reading the test:
  docs-only push (docs/sprints/1-todo/..., inside sprint 13's exclusion) -> DETECTED, commit named
  8 commits                                                             -> "5 named; ...and 3 more"
  last_shipped == tip                                                   -> None (silent)

AND YOUR OWN FLAG, CHECKED RATHER THAN TAKEN ON FAITH. You asked me to confirm your read that origin_ahead_of_record_warning already caught this before the sprint. I extracted 42a6a03^'s copy of the function and ran it against a real docs-only push: DETECTED. Your read is right, the sprint file's "existing machinery could not see it at all" is about the content comparisons specifically, and you were right to say so instead of writing code to fix something that already worked. That is the sprint-26 failure caught before it happened, which is worth more than the diff.

REQ 3's WARN-VS-REFUSE DECISION — recorded, at the call site, with the reasoning the requirement asks for: the reship cost, the high true rate of legitimate pushes on the shared branch under this framework's own parallel model, and why the identity/content check immediately above already carries the real-mismatch case. Decided, not defaulted. That is the criterion.

REQ 4 — package.json 0.2.1 -> 0.2.2, one line, nothing else in the file.

REQ 5 — three cases, and I falsified two of them rather than trusting a green run:
  neutered state_divergence_warning  -> suite FAILED ("doesn't name the other tree's phase")
  stripped the named commits         -> suite FAILED ("doesn't name the actual commit that landed")
Both tests bite. Worth knowing: the stranded-close case's first assertion (`grep -q WARNING`) still passes with the new function fully neutered, because sprint 13's sprint-file check catches that one incident by accident — your own docstring says so. The `phase 'complete'` assertion is what actually pins the new code. Not a defect, but don't let the first assertion get treated as coverage.

SUITE: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED. ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED. TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, 0.2.2.

================================================================
INFORMATIONAL, NOT BLOCKING
================================================================

- origin_ahead_of_record_warning returns None when the current branch has no upstream. Inherited from sprint 24, unchanged here, but it means Req 3's detection is silent for a role reading from a branch with no tracking config. Fine as-is; noting it so it isn't rediscovered as a regression.
- In the divergence message, phase is listed whenever the other tree has one, even when it matches, while registry status is listed only when it differs. Cosmetic asymmetry, arguably useful context. Leave it.
- Carried: every launcher allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently; who commits a QA1 verdict is still open from sprint 27.

RECOMMENDATION

Back to dev_build. Fix the early return, add the worktree-created-first case to the suite, decide what /sprint-status <id> does when only another tree holds the state, and re-run /sprint-qa1 29. Everything else here is done and I don't need to see it again.

PASS: PASS — round 2. Audited 619b07f on main. Sprint file re-read fresh and confirmed byte-identical to what I audited in round 1 (sha256 582e748d…), so this audit is scoped to what actually moved: state_divergence_warning's early return, cmd_status's single-id refusal, and the tests.

THE ROUND-1 BLOCKER IS CLOSED. I re-ran my own round-1 reproduction script unchanged against the new code — same scratch repo, same order (create in main, commit, git worktree add, then start through complete entirely inside the worktree) — and all three read commands now answer correctly instead of confidently wrong:

  /sprint-list       "1  todo" + WARNING naming the worktree path, phase 'complete', registry status 'done'
  /sprint-status     same, under the sprint's own line
  /sprint-status 1   refuses, but now says the sprint "exists in 1 other worktree(s): <path> (phase 'complete')
                     ... Read status from the tree that actually holds it" — instead of "Run /sprint-start 1 first"

That last one was the part I cared most about. Telling someone to start a sprint that's already closed isn't a missing warning, it's the framework handing out a wrong instruction at the exact moment somebody is trying to find out what happened.

SILENCE SURVIVED THE FIX, WHICH IS THE HALF THAT USUALLY BREAKS. Widening a check is easy; widening it without turning it into the banner everyone learns to scroll past is the actual work. Verified directly rather than assumed:

  worktree exists, sprint created in main, never started anywhere   -> silent, both sprints, both commands
  two sprints, one diverging and one untouched                      -> warning on the diverging one only, the other clean
  identical state across trees (round 1's case, re-run)             -> silent
  no tree anywhere holds the state                                  -> still the original "Run /sprint-start N first",
                                                                       which is the correct advice in THAT case

The `this_phase is None and this_registry_status is None` guard is what preserves that, and it is placed after the registry read rather than before it — which is exactly the ordering the round-1 bug got wrong.

REQ 1'S FAIL CRITERION — RE-CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, because round 2 added a die(). Enumerated the call sites on the new code: lines 1150 and 1214 in cmd_status, 2636 in cmd_list. All three are read-only commands, all three print. Exit codes with divergence actually present: status <id> 0, list 0, status no-id 0. Nothing refuses on divergence.

The new die() in cmd_status is not a gate on divergence and I checked the distinction properly rather than by eye. It fires only when this tree has no local state file — and in that case load_state() already died before this sprint. Divergence changes the wording, never the outcome; there is no input on which the old code succeeded and the new code refuses. Message improvement inside an already-refusing branch.

MID-LIFECYCLE DIVERGENCE, THE GENERAL CASE. Recorded a QA1 verdict in the other tree — a state-file-only write, nothing the sprint file's own check can ever see — and main surfaced "phase 'dev_build' ... other worktree (phase 'qa1_audit', registry status 'in_progress')". That is Req 1's actual ask working, not just the close case that sprint 13's file check catches by accident.

TESTS — FALSIFIED, both new ones:
  restored the round-1 early return          -> "list did not surface a sprint closed in a worktree that was never started here"
  disabled cmd_status's better refusal        -> "refusal still tells the reader to start a sprint that's already been closed elsewhere"
Both bite. And the weak assertion I flagged in round 1 is gone, replaced with the phase and path specifics that only the new code can produce, with a comment recording why — so the next person doesn't re-add a bare WARNING grep thinking it's coverage.

SUITE: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED (4 sprint-29 cases). ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED. TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED, "Installed 0.2.2".

CHANGE SURFACE: four hunks, three in state_divergence_warning and one in cmd_status, plus the tests. origin_ahead_of_record_warning is untouched between 42a6a03 and 619b07f, so round 1's Req 3 verification still stands — I confirmed the docs-only detection independently then, in my own scratch repo with a real bare origin, and nothing in this round can have moved it.

CARRIED, NOT BLOCKING
- Two cosmetic wording slips in the new message: "1 other worktree disagree" (the plural switches the noun, not the verb), and "state here shows no state file here at all" says "here" twice. Fix them whenever this function is next open; not worth a round on their own.
- If the local state file exists but is corrupt JSON, this_phase falls back to None and the message reads "no state file here at all", which isn't quite what happened. Rare, and the warning is still directionally right. Noting it so it isn't rediscovered as a mystery.
- origin_ahead_of_record_warning stays silent on a branch with no upstream (inherited from sprint 24, unchanged).
- Long-carried: every launcher allowlist entry other than git and npm remains inferred; the empty-string ownedRepository declaration still falls through silently; who commits a QA1 verdict is still Master Controller's open question from sprint 27.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 29, Pipeman ships and publishes 0.2.2. Commit this verdict first.

For LiveQA: the reproduction to run is the worktree-created-BEFORE-start order, not just the close-in-a-worktree order. Both are covered now, but the first is the one that was broken in round 1 and the one the sprint's own Team Assignments note is really about.
